prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Business software subscription pricing (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Plan" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Price" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Minimum seats" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Contract" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Support" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Plan" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Price › List price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "Price › Billing terms" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 490px
  col 4: header "Minimum seats" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Contract" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "Support" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 195px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare six business software subscription plans on headline price, billing terms, minimum seats, contract, and support so a buyer can choose a plan.","reading":"Readers scan down the Plan column and across the short comparison columns; they use List price as the quick numeric anchor, read Billing terms as explanatory prose, and compare Minimum seats, Contract, and Support as procurement constraints.","groups":["Plan is the row identifier and reading anchor.","List price and Billing terms form the Price group, but List price is a short numeric key while Billing terms is explanatory prose.","Minimum seats, Contract, and Support are short constraint/comparison columns that should be scanned together across rows."],"keep_intact":["Plan names such as Enterprise, and the Plan header","List prices such as $12 and numeric minimum-seat values","Contract terms and support-level labels, including their longest words","Headers should not break mid-word; Billing terms especially needs its full label width"],"may_wrap":["Billing terms sentences at spaces","The List price and Minimum seats headers at spaces","Longer Contract and Support phrases at spaces, never inside words"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[96,58,294,87,84,100],"idea":"Prose-first: hold every short column to its longest unbreakable word and give the surplus to Billing terms, making it the only two-line prose column."},{"name":"B","widths":[96,88,221,130,84,100],"idea":"Header-led: keep every header and row identifier on one line, then let Billing terms absorb all remaining width."},{"name":"C","widths":[105,80,180,105,105,144],"idea":"Decision matrix: balance the short comparison columns for cross-row scanning while compressing Billing terms into a compact multi-line explanatory block."}]}
